title: The morphism given by a bijective reordering of the coordinate sections is invertible
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\beta,\gamma$ be coordinate types, and let $b:\gamma\simeq\beta$ be an equivalence. Write $X=\mathbb P(\beta;S)$ [def-pc-proj], $M=(\operatorname{id}_X)^*\mathcal O_X(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-projective-space-twist], $s_j=(\operatorname{id}_X)^*T_{b(j)}$, and $U_j=D_+(T_{b(j)})$. The morphism $\phi:X\to\mathbb P(\gamma;S)$ constructed by the native homOfIsFreeGenerator from the sections $s_j$, their free-generator witnesses on $U_j$, and the cover $\bigcup_j U_j=X$, over the structure morphism $X\to S$, is an isomorphism. No finiteness or nonemptiness assumption on the coordinate types is required.

source.place: Constructions Definition 01NF and Lemma 01NE: projective-space charts and coordinate construction, applied to bijective renaming and its inverse.

proof.text: Construct psi by the native homOfIsFreeGenerator for b.symm. Apply the chart comparison for b and b.symm. On each source standard chart, the composite of the two chart isomorphisms cancels and the two affine reindexings compose to the identity: their base maps agree, and their coordinate maps are identities by the two inverse laws of b. AffineSpace.hom_ext proves this affine identity; cancellation of the chart isomorphism gives the identity on the source standard chart. Scheme.Opens.hom_ext_of_iSup_eq_top gives phi composed with psi equal to the identity globally. Repeat with b.symm for the opposite composite. This supplies the IsIso witness. The same cover argument handles empty coordinate types without choosing an index.
